The investigation must distinguish three layers with potentially different definitions of 'capacity': (a) solver constants and capacityAtSaturation() in capacity.ts; (b) WT_CAPACITY_TABLE static reference in constants.ts; (c) golden-test expected values in tests/unit/water-treatment-golden-cases.test.ts. Do not infer meaning from the function name alone; trace every call site of capacityAtSaturation to determine how its return value is used.

Pay special attention to the filtrate calculation pattern Math.max(0, input - capacity) used in computeFiltrate (test) and similar in scoring.ts. If capacity represents the maximum equilibrium dissolved concentration, assess whether subtracting it from the influent concentration is chemically and mathematically valid. Use a numerical example where influent Zn is 0.5 mg/L and the calculated saturation concentration is approximately 195 mg/L (free ion only, pH 7.5, logKsp_Zn = -15.506, pKw 13.99). Explain the expected behavior under the documented model assumptions without modifying code.

Pb solid-phase choice is open. PHREEQC and MINTEQ allow several baseline phases (Pb(OH)2, cerussite PbCO3, hydrocerussite, anglesite PbSO4) with very different Ksp values. Note which phase the current WT_SOLID_PHASE.Pb and WT_KSP_LOGK.Pb correspond to in minteq.v4.dat, and list other candidate phases that could produce values closer to the WT_CAPACITY_TABLE rows. Do not pick a different phase; just document the trade-off.
The hydroxide-only baseline is a simulation assumption, not a universal prediction for real wastewater. State this explicitly in the report so chemistry owner knows the scope.
